He played [[college basketball]] in the United States for the [[Pepperdine Waves men's basketball|Pepperdine Waves]]. ==Early career== Diawara started his career with French team [[JDA Dijon]], and after his first season in the European League, Diawara decided to attend college in the United States. He first attended junior college at [[College of Southern Idaho|Southern Idaho]], playing 63 games and averaging 12.1 points, 6.8 rebounds, 1.0 assists and 24.1 minutes while shooting 54.2 percent from the floor, 31.8 percent from three-point range and 58.6 percent from the free throw line. After two years, he transferred to [[Pepperdine University]], where he averaged 15.5 points, 6.0 rebounds, 1.0 assists and 32.5 minutes for the [[Pepperdine Waves men's basketball|Waves]], while shooting 45.6 percent from the floor, 34.3 percent from three-point range and 65 percent from the free throw line earning first-team All-[[West Coast Conference]] honors as a junior.{{cite news|title=NBA.com: Yakhouba Diawara Bio Page |url=http://www.nba.com/playerfile/yakhouba_diawara/bio.html |access-date=September 28, 2015 |work=NBA.com |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121023133927/http://www.nba.com/playerfile/yakhouba_diawara/bio.html |archive-date=October 23, 2012 }} ==Professional career== Diawara went undrafted after graduating from Pepperdine and signed with [[JDA Dijon|Dijon]] again. In February 2006, he moved to Italian team [[Fortitudo Bologna|Climamio Bologna]]. He was signed by the [[Denver Nuggets]] on 26 July 2006.{{cite news|title=Nuggets sign Yakhouba Diawara|url=http://www.insidehoops.com/diawara-nuggets-072606.shtml|access-date=July 26, 2006|work=InsideHoops.com|date=July 26, 2006}} He signed with the [[Miami Heat]] on 7 August 2008.{{cite news|title=HEAT Sign Yakhouba Diawara|url=http://www.nba.com/heat/news/heat_sign_diawara.html|access-date=August 7, 2008|work=NBA.com|date=August 7, 2008}} On 24 July 2010 Diawara signed with [[New Basket Brindisi|Enel Brindisi]] in Italy.{{cite news|title=Yakhouba Diawara inks with Enel Brindisi|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/italy/serie-a/83510/yakhouba-diawara-inks-with-enel-brindisi.html|access-date=July 24, 2010|work=Sportando.com|date=July 24, 2010}} For the 2011–12 season, he signed a one-year deal with [[Pallacanestro Varese]].{{cite news|title=Cimberio Varese announces Yakhouba Diawara|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/italy/serie-a/87633/cimberio-varese-announces-yakhouba-diawara.html|access-date=July 25, 2011|work=Sportando.com|date=July 25, 2011}} On 21 July 2012 he signed with another Italian team, [[Umana Reyer Venezia]].{{cite news|title=Venezia officially signs Diawara|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/italy/serie-a/93773/venezia-officially-signs-diawara.html|access-date=July 21, 2012|work=Sportando.com|date=July 21, 2012}} He left Venezia on 16 July 2013.{{cite news|title=Yakhouba Diawara leaves Reyer Venezia|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/italy/serie-a/103730/yakhouba-diawara-leaves-reyer-venezia.html|access-date=July 16, 2013|work=Sportando.com|date=July 16, 2013}} In September 2013, he signed a one-year deal with [[BCM Gravelines]],{{cite news|title=Yakhouba Diawara Signs One-Year Deal With BCM Gravelines Of Eurocup|url=http://basketball.realgm.com/wiretap/229832/Yakhouba-Diawara-Signs-One-Year-Deal-With-BCM-Gravelines-Of-Eurocup|access-date=September 13, 2013|work=RealGM.com|date=September 13, 2013}} however, he parted ways with them on 10 March 2014.{{cite news|title=Yakhouba Diawara leaves Gravelines-Dunkerque|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/france/113393/yakhouba-diawara-leaves-gravelines-dunkerque.html|access-date=March 10, 2014|work=Sportando.com|date=March 10, 2014}} On 21 August 2014 he returned to Cimberio Varese for the 2014–15 season.{{cite news|title=Varese announces the return of Yakhouba Diawara|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/italy/serie-a/132122/varese-announces-the-return-of-yakhouba-diawara.html|access-date=October 4, 2015|work=Sportando.com|date=August 21, 2014}} On 28 September 2015 Diawara signed with the [[Memphis Grizzlies]], returning to the NBA for the first time since 2010.{{cite news|title=Grizzlies announce 2015 training camp roster|url=http://www.nba.com/grizzlies/news/training-camp-roster-150928|access-date=September 28, 2015|work=NBA.com|date=September 28, 2015}} However, he was waived on 24 October after appearing in six preseason games.{{cite news|title=Memphis Grizzlies waive four players|url=http://www.nba.com/grizzlies/news/grizzlies-waive-players-151024|access-date=October 24, 2015|work=NBA.com|date=October 24, 2015}} On 2 November he signed with [[Limoges CSP|Limoges]] for the rest of the 2015–16 season.{{cite news|title=Limoges CSP announce Yakhouba Diawara|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/france/180771/limoges-csp-announce-yakhouba-diawara.html|access-date=November 2, 2015|work=Sportando.com|date=November 2, 2015}} On 16 January 2017 Diawara signed with Italian club [[Juvecaserta Basket]] for the rest of the [[2016–17 LBA season]].{{cite news|title=Juvecaserta agreed to terms with Yakhouba Diawara|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/italy/serie-a/223221/juvecaserta-agreed-to-terms-with-yakhouba-diawara.html|access-date=16 January 2017|work=Sportando.com|date=16 January 2017}} On 17 December 2017 Diawara signed a one-week tryout contract with Italian club [[Pistoia Basket 2000]].{{cite news|title=The Flexx Pistoia signs Yakhouba Diawara to a one-week tryout|url=https://www.sportando.com/en/italy/serie-a/257790/the-flexx-pistoia-signs-yakhouba-diawara-to-a-one-week-tryout.html|access-date=17 December 2017|work=Sportando.com|date=17 December 2017}} Four days later Pistoia announced that Diawara has passed the tryout period with the team and signed a deal for the rest of the [[2017–18 LBA season]].{{cite news|title=Pistoia Basket extends Yakhouba Diawara until the end of the season|url=https://www.sportando.com/en/italy/serie-a/258374/pistoia-basket-extends-yakhouba-diawara-until-the-end-of-the-season.html|access-date=22 December 2017|work=Sportando.com|date=22 December 2017}} ==Personal life== Diawara is the youngest of Bintou and Ansoumane Diawara's four children, having two sisters (Kankou and Fatoumata) and one brother (Sourakhata). He is fluent in [[French language|French]], [[Wolof language|Wolof]], [[English language|English]], and [[Italian language|Italian]]. ==NBA career statistics== {{NBA player statistics legend}}
